questions.question: The ________ is an embryonic midline structure common to all members of the phylum Chordata that serves as a source of midline signals to surrounding tissues and as a major skeletal element of the developing embryo.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**notochord**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **notochord** is an embryonic midline structure common to all members of the **phylum Chordata** that serves as a source of midline signals to surrounding tissues and as a major skeletal element of the developing **embryo**.
 
• The notochord, found in all members of the **phylum Chordata during embryonic development,** serves as a midline structure offering mechanical support and signaling cues.
 
• In vertebrates, it originates from the dorsal organizer and plays a vital role in ensuring proper vertebrate development.
 
• This evolutionarily conserved structure, positioned along the developing midline, delineates the primitive axis of embryos and constitutes a fundamental structural component crucial for locomotion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A nerve cord** consists of a bundle of nerve fibers that extends along the longitudinal axis of the body, serving as a crucial component of the central nervous system. 
 
• **The tail fin**, also referred to as the caudal fin, serves as the primary means of propulsion for the majority of fish species. 
 
• **The anus** marks the terminal segment of the digestive tract, situated at the conclusion of the rectum.

questions.question: In December 2021, who became the 3rd fastest Indian fast bowler to pick up 200 Test wickets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohammed Shami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohammed Shami **achieved a remarkable feat by becoming the **11th Indian bowler** to secure **200 wickets in Test cricket,** accomplishing this milestone in **just 55 test matches**.
 
• Notably, he is only the **5th Indian pace bowler** to achieve this milestone in the purest form of the game.
 
• Shami's achievement places him as the third-fastest Indian pace bowler to reach the 200-wicket mark in Test cricket.
 
• He follows in the footsteps of legendary players **Kapil Dev and Javagal Srinath, **who achieved this milestone in 50 and 54 Tests respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ishant Sharma**, a versatile Indian cricketer, has showcased his skills in Test, ODI, and T20I formats. His notable achievement came in February 2021 during a series against England, where he clinched his 300th wicket in Test cricket.
 
• **Jasprit Bumrah**, another key player for the Indian cricket team, excels across all formats. He holds the title of the fastest Indian pacer to reach 150 wickets in Test cricket. He stands as the second fastest Indian bowler to claim 100 wickets in One-Day International cricket.
 
• **Bhuvneshwar Kumar** is a former Indian international cricketer who represented the Indian cricket team from 2012 to 2022.

questions.concept: Panchayat System, Government Policies and Schemes
questions.question: Which Indian state launched the CLAP Mission on 2ⁿd October 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Andhra Pradesh **government initiated the** Clean Andhra Pradesh (CLAP)-Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam program **to enhance sanitation conditions and waste management in rural areas through community involvement.
 
• The campaign focuses on door-to-door garbage collection, segregation of liquid and solid waste, on-site waste treatment, and promoting home composting.
 
• **Chief Minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy** conducted a review meeting on the CLAP program, emphasizing its importance in the state's cleanliness initiative.
 
• **New garbage collection vehicles** were launched on July 8 to support the program's implementation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh**, situated in the **southern coastal region** of India, ranks as the **seventh-largest state **covering an area of 162,970 km2 and the tenth-most populous with 49,577,103 inhabitants.
 
• The state capital is Amaravati, while Visakhapatnam stands as its largest city. Andhra Pradesh shares borders with Telangana to the northwest, Chhattisgarh to the north, Odisha to the northeast, Tamil Nadu to the south, Karnataka to the west, and the Bay of Bengal to the east.
 
• Renowned for its extensive coastline, Andhra Pradesh boasts the second-longest coastline in India, spanning approximately 974 km. Andhra State was the first to be established on linguistic grounds in India on October 1, 1953.
 
• Subsequently, on November 1, 1956, it merged with the Telugu-speaking regions of the Hyderabad State to form Andhra Pradesh. In June 2014, the state underwent reorganization, leading to the formation of a separate Telangana state.

questions.question: ‘How I Became a Hindu’ is an autobiography of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sita Ram Goel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ‘**How I Became a Hindu’** is an autobiography of** ****Sita Ram Goel**.
 
• The book delves into **Vamadeva's (David Frawley) **personal odyssey through Veda, Vedanta, and Hindu Dharma, chronicling his extensive engagement with these subjects during his time in India.
 
• It explores his interactions with various Hindu groups and Vedic teachers spanning more than two decades.
 
• Central to the narrative is David Frawley's journey towards understanding and embracing Hindu Dharma, eventually evolving into a Hindu teacher or Hindu Dharma Pracharaka, a role that remains fundamental to all his endeavors.
 
• **Sita Ram Goel,** an eminent Indian historian, religious and political activist, writer, and publisher, is renowned for his significant contributions to Hinduism and Hindu nationalism in the latter part of the twentieth century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paramahansa Yogananda**, an Indian-American Hindu monk, yogi, and guru, introduced millions to meditation and Kriya Yoga through his organization, Self-Realization Fellowship (SRF) / Yogoda Satsanga Society (YSS) of India, the only one he established to disseminate his teachings.
 
• **Kiran Bedi**, a former tennis player, made history by becoming the first woman in India to join the officer ranks of the Indian Police Service (IPS) in 1972. She served as the 24th Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry from May 28, 2016, to February 16, .2021
 
• **Kamala Surayya**, known by her one-time pen name Madhavikutty and her married name Kamala Das, was an Indian poet in English and an author in Malayalam from Kerala, India.

questions.question: Which form of government is established by the Constitution of India both, at the centre and states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliamentary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Constitution** institutes a** parliamentary system** of governance at **both the central and state levels,** presenting a federal structure with certain unitary characteristics.
 
• It draws its foundation from the Westminster model, entrusting control over finances to elected representatives in adherence to the principle of **"no taxation without representation."**
 
• Within a federal framework, authority is divided between the central and state governments, a delineation clearly outlined in the Indian Constitution concerning legislative powers.
 
• The Constitution proclaims India as a sovereign democratic republic, encompassing an autonomous judiciary, safeguarded fundamental rights, and directive principles of state policy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A Council of Ministers,** led by the **Chief Minister, **advises the Governor in Indian governance and administration at the central, state, and local levels.
 
• This section offers insights into the Constitution of India, the functioning of Parliament and Legislature, Union administration, as well as state, district, and local administration.

questions.question: In hockey, if the umpire indicates the direction with one arm raised horizontally, it means _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free hit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In field hockey,** when an** umpire raises one arm** horizontally and holds it at face level, it signifies a free hit.
 
• The signal denotes the direction of play, **limited to 10 meters**.
 
• When both arms are pointed horizontally toward the center of the field, it indicates a goal scored.
 
• Conversely, raising both arms horizontally in the direction of the goal signifies a penalty corner.
 
• **A penalty corner **is awarded for defensive violations within the penalty circle or willful violations within the defensive 23-meter zone.
 
• Often referred to as a short corner, it offers attacking players a prime opportunity to score.
 
• During penalty corners, players employ specialized skills like the drag flick, and specific rules exclusive to this phase of the game come into play.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"hockey"** encompasses a diverse array of team games played across various surfaces such as outdoor** fields, ice rinks, or dry gymnasium floors**.
 
• Despite differences in regulations, player counts, attire, and playing fields, these games all involve two opposing teams using sticks to maneuver a ball or disc towards a goal.
 
• Hockey exists in multiple forms, with some variants incorporating skates while others do not.
 
• Additional descriptors like "field hockey," "ice hockey," "roller hockey," "rink hockey," or "floor hockey" are often appended to the term "hockey" to differentiate between these distinct variations.

questions.question: What type of climate occurs along the west coast of continents in subtropical latitudes between 30° - 40° latitudes, covering Central California, Central Chile along the coast in South East and South Western Australia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mediterranean climate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mediterranean climate** occurs along the western coasts of continents within **subtropical latitudes**, typically ranging between** 30° and 40° latitudes.**
 
• This climate is evident in regions such as **Central California, Central Chile, and the coastal areas of South-Eastern and South-Western Australia.**
 
• In this climate zone, winters are generally mild and summers are warm, with significant temperature variations among different regions.
 
• Rainfall is irregular, with the majority occurring during the winter months.
 
• Common vegetation in Mediterranean climates includes oaks, olives, citrus fruits, and junipers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Subtropical steppes** are situated in the transitional areas between dry and humid climates, receiving slightly more precipitation than subtropical deserts. This amount is adequate to support sparse grasslands.
 
• **A humid subtropical climate** is characterized by hot, humid summers and cool to mild winters, falling within the temperate category.
 
• **The marine west coast climate** is typically found midway between the tropics and the Arctic or Antarctic regions, typically between 35 and 60 degrees north latitude.

questions.question: Who among the following has been credited with taking the shehnai from the marriage mandap to the concert hall?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ustad Bismillah Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan** is widely recognized for elevating the **shehnai from wedding ceremonies to the concert stage, **pioneering its integration into Indian classical music.
 
• His groundbreaking performance at the Calcutta All India Music Conference in 1937 marked the shehnai's emergence as a prominent instrument in the classical music realm.
 
• Throughout his illustrious career, Khan garnered numerous accolades and honors, including the **Padma Vibhushan (1980), Padma Bhushan (1968), Padma Shri (1961), and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1956).**
 
• In 2001, Ustad Bismillah Khan achieved the remarkable distinction of becoming the third classical musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ali Ahmed Hussain Khan** was a renowned shehnai maestro from India.
 
• **Rajendra Prasanna,** hailing from the Benares Gharana, is a prominent Indian classical flautist and shehnai player. He was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Hindustani Instrumental Music in 2017.
 
• **Anant Lal, **commonly addressed with the title Pandit, was a distinguished Indian classical musician known for his mastery of the shehnai. In 1989, he was bestowed with the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the highest recognition for artists in India.

questions.question: ‘Dzongkha’ is the official language of which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhutan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dzongkha**, a **Sino-Tibetan language**, holds the distinction of being the official and national **language of Bhutan**. It employs the **Tibetan script **for its written form.
 
• The term** "dzongkha" **translates to "the language of the fortress," derived from "dzong" meaning "fortress" and "kha" meaning "language."
 
• As of 2013, Dzongkha boasted **171,080 native speakers** and approximately 640,000 speakers overall.
 
• Belonging to the South Tibetic language group, Dzongkha shares close linguistic ties and partial intelligibility with Sikkimese, as well as with other Bhutanese languages such as Chocha Ngacha, Brokpa, Brokkat, and Lakha.
 
• While it maintains a more distant relationship with Standard Tibetan, spoken Dzongkha and Tibetan exhibit mutual intelligibility ranging from 50 to 80 percent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhutan**, officially known as the **Kingdom of Bhutan,** is a landlocked country located in South Asia, nestled in the **Eastern Himalayas **between China to the north and India to the south.
 
• It encompasses a population of over 727,145 people and spans a territory of 38,394 square kilometers.
 
• Bhutan ranks 133rd globally in terms of land area and 160th in terms of population. As a constitutional monarchy, Bhutan is governed by a king, known as the Druk Gyalpo, who serves as the head of state, while a prime minister leads the government. Vajrayana Buddhism holds the status of the state religion, with the Je Khenpo serving as the spiritual leader.
 
• Both Bhutan and its neighboring region of Tibet have witnessed the propagation of Buddhism, originating from the Indian subcontinent during the era of Gautama Buddha.

questions.question: In which year did the Election Commission of India for the first time in its history become multimember body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1989**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Election Commission of India (ECI) **underwent a structural change from being a single-member body, with only the **Chief Election Commissioner,** from its establishment in **1950 until October 1989.**
 
• Following the **Election Commissioner Amendment Act 1989**, it evolved into a multi-member body.
 
• Since October 1989 to the present day, it has comprised three members: **one Chief Election Commissioner and two election commissioners.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Established by the **Constitution of India, the ECI **is a constitutional body tasked with **conducting and regulating elections across the country.**
 
• **Article 324 of the Constitution** vests the commission with the authority for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to parliament, state legislatures, the offices of the president and vice-president of India.
 
• Thus, the Election Commission functions as an all-India body, overseeing elections at both the central and state levels.
 
• The commission administers elections for various bodies, including the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, State Legislative Councils, and the offices of the President and Vice President.
 
• Operating under the authority of the Constitution, as per Article 324, it is further guided by the Representation of the People Act.

questions.concept: States Affairs, Government Policies and Schemes
questions.question: Who among the following announced the ‘Sushma Swaraj Award’ for women in the state budget in 2022?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Haryana Chief Minister, Manohar Lal Khattar** introduced the **'Sushma Swaraj Award' **during the state budget presentation, honoring women for their noteworthy achievements and contributions in various fields at both national and international levels.
 
• The award, named after the late Sushma Swaraj, a former lawyer of the Supreme Court and prominent Indian politician, will carry a prize of Rs 5 lakh along with a commendation.
 
• Sushma Swaraj, a senior member of the Bharatiya Janata Party, served as India's Minister of External Affairs during the** first Narendra Modi government (2014–2019)**, becoming the second woman to hold this position after Indira Gandhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.concept: Science Technology and Inventions, Awards and Honours
questions.question: Hideki Yukawa, who received the Nobel Prize in 1949, is well known for which discovery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Theory of nuclear forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hideki Yukawa **is renowned for his **groundbreaking theory of nuclear forces,** particularly his prediction of the **existence of mesons**.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1949** for this significant contribution to the field.
 
• In 1935,** Yukawa **published his theory of mesons, elucidating the interactions between protons and neutrons.
 
• His theory was inspired by the discovery of a specific type of meson in cosmic rays by American physicists in **1937**.
 
• Yukawa's work established him as one of the most influential theoretical physicists of the 20th century and earned him the distinction of being Japan's first Nobel laureate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meghnad Saha,** an Indian astrophysicist, is renowned for his development of the theory of thermal ionization in 1920. Thermal ionization is a physical phenomenon wherein atoms are desorbed from a heated surface and subsequently ionized.
 
• **Homi Jehangir Bhabha**, an Indian nuclear scientist, is celebrated for his research on the cascade process of cosmic radiation. This process involves a sequence of secondary interactions occurring when cosmic rays collide with air nuclei in the upper atmosphere.
 
• **Alessandro Volta** is credited as the first individual to create an electric charge storage device using metal disks and acid-dipped cardboard. This invention laid the foundation for the development of the standard unit of electric charge in the International System of Units (SI), known as the coulomb (C).

questions.question: Who among the following was conferred with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pramod Bhagat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pramod Bhagat** was conferred with the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021**.
 
• Pramod Bhagat, born on June 4, 1988, is an accomplished Indian professional **Para-badminton** player hailing from the Vaishali district of Bihar.
 
• He currently holds the **world number 2 ranking in para-badminton men's singles** SL3 and clinched a gold medal at the 2020 Summer Paralympics in Men's singles SL3.
 
• His achievements have been recognized with several prestigious awards:
 
 
• **2019: Arjuna Award**
 
• **2019: Biju Patnaik Sports Award,** Odisha
 
• **2021: Khel Ratna Award,** the highest sporting honour in India
 
• **2022: Padma Shri,** one of India's highest civilian honours
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Khel Ratna Award, **officially known as the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award,** stands as India's highest sporting honour.
 
• Presented annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, this prestigious award was renamed in honour of Major Dhyan Chand, an iconic Indian field hockey player known for his exceptional career spanning over 20 years from 1926 to 1948, during which he scored more than 1000 goals.
 
• The inaugural recipient of the award was chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand, recognized for his outstanding performance during the year 1991–92.
 
• Notably, in 2001, sport shooter Abhinav Bindra made history as the youngest recipient of the award at the age of 18.

questions.question: Pottery was first traceable to which period of ancient Indian history?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neolithic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pottery** was first traceable to the **Neolithic period of ancient Indian history**.
 
• Pottery encompasses both the process and the resulting objects formed from clay and other ceramic materials.
 
• It involves shaping a ceramic body into desired forms and then subjecting them to high temperatures in a bonfire, pit, or kiln.
 
• This ancient craft is among the oldest human inventions, dating back thousands of years.
 
• The oldest known pottery, originating from the **Neolithic revolution** approximately 10,000 years ago, serves as evidence of its early development.
 
• The Greeks are acknowledged for elevating pottery to an art form, showcasing intricate designs and techniques that continue to inspire today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Neolithic or New Stone Age, **derived from the Greek words for "new" and "stone," denotes an archaeological epoch and the final segment of the Stone Age across Europe, Asia, and Africa.
 
• It witnessed the Neolithic Revolution, a series of developments such as farming, animal domestication, and the transition from a hunter-gatherer lifestyle to settled communities.
 
• Coined by Sir John Lubbock in 1865, the term "Neolithic" refined the three-age system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Chalcolithic period**, also known as the Copper Age, served as a transitional phase from the Neolithic to the Bronze Age.
 
• **The Palaeolithic, or Paleolithic,** denotes a prehistoric era beginning approximately 3.3 million years ago and concluding around 11,650 years ago.
 
• **The Mesolithic, or Middle Stone Age**, refers to an archaeological epoch lasting from approximately 10,000 to 5,000 BC.

questions.concept: Diversity in The Living World, Biology, Sewage
questions.question: Which is a multicellular filamentous green alga consisting of thin unbranched chains of cylindrical cells and found in floating masses near the surface of streams and ponds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spirogyra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spirogyra** is a multicellular filamentous** green alga consisting of thin unbranched chains of cylindrical cells **and found in floating masses near the surface of streams and ponds.
 
• Spirogyra, belonging to the genus Spirogyra, encompasses approximately 400 species of free-floating green algae found in freshwater environments globally.
 
• Named for their distinctive spiral chloroplasts, spirogyras are filamentous algae composed of **thin, unbranched chains of cylindrical cells.**
 
• These algae often form masses that float near the surface of streams and ponds, buoyed by oxygen bubbles produced during photosynthesis.
 
• They are frequently employed in laboratory demonstrations. Spirogyra species reproduce both sexually and asexually.
 
• Asexual, or vegetative, reproduction occurs through the simple fragmentation of the filaments.
 
• Sexual reproduction takes place through a process called conjugation, wherein cells from two filaments lying adjacent to each other become connected through outgrowths known as conjugation tubes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ectocarpus** is a genus of filamentous brown algae renowned as a model organism for studying the genomics of multicellularity.
 
• **Laminaria**, commonly referred to as kelp, is a genus of brown seaweed characterized by its large and intricate structure. Native to the northern Pacific and north Atlantic Oceans, Laminaria is a significant component of marine ecosystems.
 
• **Chlorella** comprises approximately thirteen species of single-celled green algae within the division Chlorophyta.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Tamu Lachar festival celebrated as the New Year by the Gurung Community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sikkim** observes the **Tamu Lochar festival, **which is the** New Year celebration of the Gurung community,** on** December 30th **annually.
 
• This festival signifies the transition of the** animal sign (lho) for the Gurung people.**
 
• **Tamu Lochar **stands as a significant festival for the Hindu Nepalese community in Sikkim, believed to have ancient origins predating Buddhism in the region.
 
• Festivities include elaborate feasts featuring traditional Gurung cuisine and the exchange of warm greetings among individuals.
 
• Primarily celebrated by Nepalese Buddhists, particularly the Gurung ethnic group, the festival is centered around monasteries.
 
• It commences with families and relatives visiting these sacred sites, offering prayers, and performing rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Gurung people **are an indigenous ethnic group residing in the hills and mountains of **Gandaki Province, Nepal.**
 
• As one of the prominent Gurkha tribes, they are estimated to comprise around 200,000 individuals.
 
• Primarily situated on the southern side of the Annapūrna mountain massif, the Gurung predominantly inhabit districts such as Manang, Mustang, Dolpo, Kaski, Lamjung, Gorkha, Parbat, Tanahun, and Syangja.
 
• Speaking a Tibeto-Burman language, the Gurung community is largely followers of Lamaist Buddhism, although some have embraced Hinduism.
 
• They possess a vibrant cultural heritage, characterized by a rich tradition of folk music and dance, which holds significant importance in their cultural practices.

questions.question: Surupa Sen is a famous _________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surupa Sen,** an accomplished** Odissi dancer **and choreographer, has dedicated her career to the art form while residing and working in Nrityagram, a renowned dance village located in **rural Karnataka, India.**
 
• Her journey in Odissi commenced two decades ago under the** tutelage of Guru Kelucharan Mahapatra, the eminent architect of Odissi.**
 
• Surupa honed her skills under the guidance of Guru Protima Gauri, Guru Ratikant Mahapatra, and Guru Bichitranandan Swain. Throughout her illustrious career, Surupa has been recognized with several prestigious awards.
 
• These include the Raza Foundation Award in 2006, the Yagnaraman Award from Sri Krishna Gana Sabha, Chennai in 2008, the Nritya Choodamani from Sri Krishna Gana Sabha, Chennai in 2011, and the esteemed Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Odissi Dance in 2018. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Odissi**, a classical Indian dance, finds its roots in the ancient temples of Odisha, a coastal state in eastern India.
 
• **Kathak**, one of the eight principal forms of Indian classical dance, traces its origins to the wandering bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakar or storytellers.
 
• **Kathakali **is a classical Indian dance-drama that emerged from the state of Kerala in southwestern India.
 
• **Bharatanatyam, **another classical Indian dance form, originated in the state of Tamil Nadu, India.

questions.question: Some of Swami Dayanand’s followers started a network of schools and colleges called D.A.V. What does ‘A’ stand for in D.A.V.?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anglo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Trust and Management Society** was founded in **1886 **to fulfil the visionary ideals of the eminent philosopher **Maharishi Dayanand Saraswati**.
 
• It was officially registered under the **Societies Act of 1860.**
 
• The inaugural DAV School was established in Lahore during the same year, with Mahatma Hansraj serving as the Honorary Headmaster.
 
• The DAV family encompasses 900 schools, 75 colleges, and a university.
 
• The "DAV Movement," initiated in 1886 by Lala Lajpat Rai (acknowledged as the Father of the DAV Movement), gained significant traction thanks to the dedicated efforts of individuals such as Mahatma Hans Raj, Pandit Gurudutt Vidyarthi, and numerous other committed Arya Samaj activists. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dayanand Saraswati,** a Hindu philosopher and social leader, is renowned as the founder of the Arya Samaj, a reform movement within Hinduism.
 
• His seminal work,** "Satyarth Prakash," **stands as a significant text elucidating Vedic philosophy and delineating human responsibilities.
 
• In 1876, he issued a groundbreaking call for Swaraj, advocating "India for Indians," a sentiment later echoed by Lokmanya Tilak. Rejecting idolatry and ritualistic practices, he aimed to revive the pure ideologies of the Vedas.
 
• Esteemed figures such as philosopher and former President of India, S. Radhakrishnan, along with Sri Aurobindo, recognized him as one of the key architects of Modern India.

questions.question: Who among the following won the ‘World Choreography Award 2020’ ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suresh Mukund**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Suresh Mukund, **an** Emmy Award-nominated Indian choreographer**, made history by winning the 10th Annual** 'World Choreography Award 2020',** also known as Choreo Awards, becoming the first Indian to achieve this prestigious honor.
 
• His victory came in the 'TV REALITY SHOW/COMPETITION' category for his exceptional work on the popular American TV reality show** 'World of Dance'**.
 
• Mukund serves as the director and choreographer of the renowned Indian dance crew 'The Kings', which secured victory in the 2019 season of World of Dance.
 
• The World Choreography Awards, often dubbed as the **"Oscars of Dance," **are held annually in Los Angeles, spotlighting the most innovative and original works by top choreographers featured in television, film, commercials, digital content, and music videos. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Geeta Kapur **is an Indian choreographer and television personality known for her contributions to the dance industry.
 
• **Prabhu Deva** is an acclaimed Indian dance choreographer, film director, producer, and actor renowned for his work in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada language films. Over his 32-year career, he has established unique dancing styles and earned two National Film Awards for Best Choreography.
 
• **Farah Khan Kunder** is a versatile Indian filmmaker, writer, producer, actress, dancer, and choreographer, primarily active in Hindi cinema.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The World Choreography Awards (WCA)** is a global awards ceremony honoring choreographic excellence in various media formats. The WCA acknowledges and celebrates original and innovative dance creations showcased in television, film, music videos, digital content, and commercials.

questions.question: Raichur doab, the land between Krishna and Tungabhadra was a region of conflict between the kings of Vijayanagar and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahamani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raichur doab**, the land between **Krishna and Tungabhadra **was a reason for conflict between **the kings of Vijayanagar and Bahamani.**
 
• **The Raichur-Tungabhadra Doab region** was a frequent battleground between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms.
 
• Situated in the southern Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, the Raichur Doab is a triangular landmass between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.
 
• Both kingdoms sought control over this region due to its wealth and economic resources.
 
• With ambitious and formidable rulers, they aimed to annex and assert dominance over each other's territories.
 
• Religious differences further fueled the conflict, as the majority of the southern population adhered to Hinduism, while the northern populace followed Islam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Bahmani Sultanate** was a Muslim empire that governed the Deccan Plateau in South India.
 
• **Malwa** is a historical region situated in west-central India, encompassing a plateau of volcanic origin.
 
• **Golconda** is a fortified citadel and abandoned city situated in the western outskirts of Hyderabad, Telangana, India.
 
• **The Bengal Sultanate** was a late medieval sultanate established in the Bengal region during the 14th to 16th century.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the characteristic features of the Indian Desert?

options.text: It is also known as Marusthali.
It lies northwest of the Aravalli hills.
It receives 250 mm rainfall per year.

questions.solution:
The current answer is __**It receives 250 mm rainfall per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The defining characteristics of the** Indian Desert** include its vast expanse of **sand dunes and an annual rainfall of less than 150 mm**. 
 
• Situated between the** Aravalli Mountains** and the plains formed by the **Sutlej and Indus rivers**, it's also known as the **Thar Desert**. 
 
• Comprised mainly of rocks and sand, it exhibits a harsh, dry climate, with temperatures ranging from near freezing to a** scorching 50°C**. 
 
• Despite the challenging conditions, some areas experience a fleeting spring season. 
 
• This region, although densely populated, presents a formidable environment for human, plant, and animal survival compared to other landscapes. 
 
• Millet stands out as the primary crop cultivated in the Indian Desert.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Thar Desert, **also referred to as the** Great Indian Desert,** sprawls across the north-western region of the Indian subcontinent, spanning approximately 200,000 km² (77,000 sq mi) across India and Pakistan.
 
• Ranking as the **18th largest desert **globally and the 9th largest hot subtropical desert, it boasts an arid and subtropical climate.
 
• Temperature fluctuations are notable between seasons, ranging from near-freezing in winter to over 50°C during the summer months.
 
• Annual rainfall averages between 100 to 500 mm, primarily occurring in the brief July-to-September southwest monsoon period.
 
• The desert comprises a distinctly dry area, Marusthali, in the west, contrasted by a semidesert section in the east, characterized by fewer sand dunes and slightly increased precipitation.

questions.question: As per the 2011 Census, what percentage of the total population in India lives in rural areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**68.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2011 Census** indicates that** 68.84% of India's population** resided in** rural areas**, while only 31.16% lived in urban areas.
 
• This discrepancy is attributed to India's agrarian history, with many engaged in agricultural pursuits.
 
• Rapid urbanization and migration for employment have contributed to the urban population's growth, albeit at a slower pace than rural areas.
 
• Disparities in infrastructure and amenities between rural and urban regions further influence population distribution trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **2011 census of India,** also known as the 15th Indian census, occurred in two stages: house listing and population enumeration.
 
• The house listing phase commenced on April 1, 2010, focusing on gathering information about all buildings and also collecting data for the National Population Register (NPR), which aims to assign a unique 12-digit identification number to all Indian residents.
 
• The second phase, population enumeration, took place between February 9 and 28, 2011.
 
• This census marked the first instance of collecting biometric information since the census's inception in 1872.

questions.question: In 1948, Ernest Mackay mentioned that in the Harappan city of Lothal, the drains for the drainage system were made of _______ bricks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**burnt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1948, Ernest Mackay **mentioned that in the **Harappan city of Lothal**, the drains for the drainage system were made of **burnt bricks**.
 
• **Ernest Mackay's **findings on the drainage system in Lothal reveal the advanced urban planning and engineering skills of the **ancient Harappan civilization.**
 
• The drains, constructed with burnt bricks and mortar, were meticulously crafted with smooth, seamless joints.
 
• They featured removable bricks for easy cleaning, along with drops at regular intervals to facilitate automatic cleaning.
 
• This systematic approach demonstrated the Harappans' sophisticated understanding of sanitation and urban infrastructure, showcasing their remarkable organizational abilities and technological prowess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ernest John Henry Mackay**, a** British archaeologist** hailing from Bristol, gained recognition for his excavations and research on **Mohenjo-daro **and other sites associated with the Indus Valley civilization.
 
• **During World War I, Mackay** served as a **captain in the Royal Army Medical Corps** in Egypt and Palestine, notably with the Imperial Camel Corps.
 
• In 1919, he participated in an Army Commission tasked with surveying ancient monuments in Palestine and Syria.
 
• Following this, from 1919 to 1922, he held the position of Custodian of Antiquities for the Palestine government.
 
• Mackay's notable contributions include his extensive excavations at Mohenjo-daro, a city flourishing between 2500 BC and 1900 BC.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers of British India is known as Lokhitwadi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Hari Deshmukh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rao Bahadur Gopal Hari Deshmukh**, also known as** Lokhitwadi,** was a prominent Indian activist, thinker, social reformer, and writer hailing from Maharashtra.
 
• Originally bearing the surname Shidhaye, his family came to be known as Deshmukh due to the **'Vatan' **(tax collection rights) they received.
 
• Deshmukh is celebrated as a significant figure of the* Social Reform ***Movement in Maharashtra**.
 
• His professional journey commenced as a translator for the government during the British Raj era.
 
• In 1867, he was appointed as a small cause judge in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, followed by a tenure as a Diwan in Ratlam state.
 
• Acknowledging his contributions, the government bestowed upon him the honorifics of 'Justice of Peace' and 'Raobahadur' during his tenure. He concluded his career as a sessions judge upon retirement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bal Gangadhar Shastri Jambhekar**, hailed as the Father of Marathi journalism, is credited for pioneering journalism in the Marathi language. His significant contribution includes the establishment of the first Marathi newspaper, 'Darpan,' during the initial years of British rule in India.
 
• **Dadoba Pandurang**, a luminary from Bombay, was a notable social reformer and linguist known for his contributions.
 
• **Gopal Ganesh Agarkar,** another eminent figure from Bombay Presidency, British India, was revered as a social reformer, educationist, and profound thinker, leaving a lasting impact on society.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a minor industrial region of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hugli region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hugli region** is **NOT **an example of a** minor industrial region of India.**
 
• The Hooghly region encompasses a sprawling industrial zone spanning **2,000 square kilometers** along the** banks of the Hooghly River **in India, stretching from** Bansberia in the north to Birlanagar in the south.**
 
• It constitutes India's oldest and second-largest industrial area, known as the Hooghly Industrial Belt.
 
• Situated in West Bengal, approximately 40 kilometers north of Kolkata, the Hooghly district derives its name from the Hooghly River, which flows along its western bank.
 
• Renowned for its economic prosperity, the district serves as a prominent center for jute cultivation, jute industry, and jute trade within the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ambala-Amritsar industrial region,** situated in the states of Haryana and Punjab, is a minor industrial area in India.
 
• **The North Malabar region** in Kerala, India, is also recognized as a minor industrial zone.
 
• **Minor Industrial Regions in India** are:
 
 
• Ambala-Amritsar in Haryana-Punjab.
 
• Saharanpur-Muzaffarnagar-Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Indore-Dewas-Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Jaipur-Ajmer in Rajasthan.
 
• Kolhapur-South Kannada in Maharashtra-Karnataka.
 
• Northern Malabar in Kerala.
 
• Middle Malabar in Kerala.
 
• Adilabad-Nizamabad in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Allahabad-Varanasi-Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Bhojpur-Munger in Bihar.
